# Vattakkhandhaka (Kd 18)

**ID:** Kd 18  
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Vattakkhandhaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m3.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m3.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vattakkhandhaka* (Kd 18) is the eighth chapter of the *Cullavagga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka, focusing on proper monastic conduct and etiquette (*vatta*, etymologically connected to Sanskrit *vṛtta* or *vrata*) [Collins; Norman 1983; Entrance to the Vinaya 1969]. It details the behavioral duties and reciprocal observances governing monks in various communal and daily scenarios, including relations between preceptor and pupil, protocols for incoming, resident, and departing monks, and decorum during alms rounds, forest dwelling, and within dining halls, living quarters, restrooms, and saunas. Unlike many other Khandhaka chapters that organize ecclesiastical legal procedures, the *Vattakkhandhaka* contains no formal ecclesiastical acts (*karmavācanā*); rather, its regulations pertain primarily to *abhisamācāra* (minor rules of proper behavior and deportment), displaying close thematic connections with the *sekhiya* training rules [Sung 1999; Entrance to the Vinaya 1969].

 In the Mūlasarvāstivādin tradition, much of this material is incorporated within the *Kṣudrakavastu* [Clarke]. English translation includes that of Bhikkhu Brahmali.

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: san-mu-kd18c Vatta; xct-mu-kd18c Vatta; lzh-mu-kd18c Vatta; Lzh Sarv Kd17c c. Vatta Khandhaka; Lzh Dg Kd 18 Vatta Khandhaka; Lzh Mi Kd 14 Vatta Khandhaka
- Passage-level parallels: Kd 1 Mahākhandhaka

**Sources**

- [Clarke] Shayne Clarke, 'Vinayas', in Brill's Encyclopedia of Buddhism — Information on the correspondence between Vattakkhandhaka and the Mūlasarvāstivāda Kṣudrakavastu.
- [Collins] Steven Collins, 'On the Very Idea of the Pali Canon' — Etymological note on vatta (< Skt vṛtta / vrata) and khandhakavatta.
- [Entrance to the Vinaya 1969] Entrance to the Vinaya: Vinayamukha, Vol. 1 (1969) — Characterization of the Vattakkhandhaka in the Cullavagga as treating abhisamācāra rules connected to the Sekhiyavatta.
- [Norman 1983] K. R. Norman, Pali Literature (Wiesbaden: Otto Harrassowitz, 1983) — Enumeration and translation of the title as 'Observances' within the Khandhaka collection.
- [Prebish 1994] Charles S. Prebish, Survey of Vinaya Literature (1994) — Correlation between Vattakkhandhaka and the Ācāravastu.
- [Sung 1999] Kang-yuan Sung, 'Tradition and Development in the Mo-ho-seng-ch’i-lu (Mahāsāṃghika)' (PhD diss., 1999) — Observations on the absence of karmavācanā in Vattakkhandhaka and concordances with Mahāsāṃghika Vinaya.
